subject: Hosted API: low-volume pilot pricing & ops fee structure
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: Hosted API minimums for a small pilot

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. We want to run a 2–3 month pilot of an LLM assistant inside BrightPath (clinical triage help desk). Expected traffic is very light to start — roughly 80k–120k tokens/month while we integrate and validate outputs.

Two quick questions so we can budget:
- What are your minimum monthly spend or commit options for Hosted API customers who won’t take Dedicated?
- Do you have a small-customer pilot path (credits or a low retainer) that protects us from an early-term commitment but gives predictable rates if we convert?

Our compliance folks may ask about data retention and logs; we can share the specifics if needed, but for now we just want the pricing/packaging options and any minimums.

Attached is a short one-pager that outlines our use case.

Cheers,
Samantha Reed
Head of Product
BrightPath Health

Attachments: brightpath_product_onepager.pdf (PDF, 430KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API minimums for a small pilot

Hi Samantha — great to meet you yesterday. Appreciate the one-pager, that helps. TL;DR: we have two pragmatic paths for small pilots on Hosted (no Dedicated required):

1) Pay-as-you-go (no monthly commit)
   - Per-token billing at our standard hosted rates; no up-front monthly minimum.
   - Good for very unpredictable usage; can burst but price is slightly higher than committed rates.

2) Starter Operational Fee (low monthly retainer) + reduced per-token rate
   - Example structure we can offer for pilots of this size: $1,500/month ops fee for the pilot period (30–90 days) + per-token rate of $0.00065/token.
   - Ops fee nets you a small reserved pool (priority scheduling, 95th-percentile burst protection) and 1,500,000 tokens of credit applied each month of the pilot.
   - If you exceed the credited tokens, additional usage will bill at the discounted per-token rate above.
   - If you convert to a committed plan within 90 days, we can apply the ops fees as a credit toward the first month and offer a conversion discount (example: 12% further discount on committed tiers for the first 6 months).

Notes and customization:
- We can lower the ops fee to $1,000/mo if you need a smaller entry price, but that reduces the token credit to ~1,000,000 tokens/month.
- We also offer a pure trial credit (one-time $3k credit) for qualifying strategic pilots — typically tied to a short conversion window and basic operational details (SLA expectations, no regulated PHI storage without Private deployment).

Can you confirm which of the following you prefer so I can get an official quote and a short term-sheet?
A) No-commit PAYG (send rates + rate card)
B) Starter ops fee: $1,500/mo + credits (or $1,000 lower option)
C) One-time trial credit + PAYG

Also: quick ask for your team — expected 95th percentile concurrency (requests/sec) and whether you'll need HIPAA-level controls during the pilot. If you need HIPAA, we should bring in Security early because Hosted has controls but Private or Dedicated can sometimes be required depending on the ingestion/post-processing flows.

I’ve looped in Aditya (cc) who handles pilot commercials and can help with an approval path if we need to move to a discounted pilot credit.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the clear options — really helpful. A few follow-ups from our side:
- Our early budget for the pilot is closer to $1,000/month total, so the $1,500 ops fee is above what we’ve carved out. If you can do the $1,000 ops fee + 1M token credit path, that would be much easier for budgeting.
- We’d prefer the ops-fee + discounted rate route (B) because predictable credits + a small monthly commitment helps our procurement team.
- Burst tolerance: we do need occasional spikes (short bursts to 10–12 rps), so priority scheduling would be important.
- HIPAA: the pilot will avoid storing PHI in the model output store for now; compliance will want to sign off on logs/retention post-PoC.

If you can send a short term-sheet that shows: $1,000/mo ops fee, token credit, per-token rate, pilot length (60–90 days), and conversion mechanics (credit application + any conversion discount), I can push to procurement and legal.

I’ve attached a draft SOW that we use for pilots (internal template) — it’s a starting point.

Thanks,
Samantha

Attachments: BrightPath_Pilot_SOW_draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Subject: Internal: BrightPath pilot — approve $1k starter ops fee + conversion path?

Folks — quick internal note on BrightPath (deal BP-2026-P1):

Recap: Prospect wants a 60–90 day pilot, ~1M tokens/month baseline, occasional spikes to ~12rps. They prefer a predictable small fee rather than pure PAYG.

Proposed commercial we can offer to close:
- Starter Ops Fee: $1,000/month for pilot term (60 days preferred).
- Token credit: 1,000,000 tokens/month applied as usage credit.
- Overages billed at $0.00070/token (discounted hosted rate).
- Conversion: if BrightPath signs a 12-month committed Hosted plan within 90 days, apply all ops fees as a credit to first invoice and provide an additional 10% conversion discount on committed per-token rates for first 6 months.
- Trial credit alternative: we can offer a one-time $2,500 trial credit instead of lowering the ops fee if legal prefers less contractual language.

Asks: Aditya — ok to approve $1k ops fee + the 10% conversion discount? Marissa — if legal signs off on the SOW template, do we need to route to Sales Ops for an exception?

If everyone is good, I’ll send a one-page term-sheet to Samantha and attach our pilot SOW. We should aim to land this pilot quickly — small ARR but good case study potential in healthcare.

Neha
